text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Four deputy commanders of the air base near Panevezhys refused to obey a newly-appointed commander.
- Customs department officals have said that the head and deputies of the Vilnius customs office should resing to improve the struggle against smuggling.

- Grigishkes paper producer mill reported a profit of 2.1 million litas in 1996 versus 4.5 million litas a year before. The company's shareholders meeting decided to keep all the profit within the firm.

- Cigarette giant British American Tobacco BAT.L aims at a bigger stake of Lithuania's cigarette market this year. Last year, BAT had 1.5 percent of the market. Nearly 85 percent of the country's market is controlled by Philip Morris.
- State-run Marijampole Tinned Milk intends to issue 20 million litas of shares and to look for foreign investors.
- Lithuanian Poles Election Action celebrates a sure victory in Vilnius and Shalchininkai regions' municipalities.

- Vilnius and Hermis banks, Rokishkis Cheese and Medienos Plaushas have applied to be included into the official trading list of Vilnius bourse. Trade on the official list is expected to start on April 7.

- Lithuania's Social Democrats may ask for a referendum on the privatisation of the country's stategic companies such as Lithuanian Telecom, Klaipeda sea port comapnies and Butinges Nafta oil terminal.
- Swedish PEAB Ost AB started reconstruction works worth $11 million on the Astorija hotel in Vilnius centre. It is expected that the four star hotel will be opened in October.
